title: Exploring attitudes and stigma toward using and not using antipsychotic medication. A multilevel cross-cultural study.
summary:
Background and Rationale: Research has shown that, in addition to weighing the benefits and risks, the fear of stigmatization also influences individuals’ decisions regarding the use or non-use of antipsychotics. In this context, individuals are potentially confronted with two different types of stigmatization: on the one hand, if they decide to take antipsychotics, and on the other hand, if they choose not to take them, discontinue them, or reduce their dosage. In addition, several stakeholders—those affected, their relatives, and psychiatrists—are involved in the decision-making process and the stigmatization process, and thus have the potential to influence the process.
Objectives: The study aims to investigate differences in attitudes and stigmatization related to the use or non-use of antipsychotics, as well as the influence of this (self-)stigma on the decision of those affected to use or not use antipsychotics. The aim is to 1.) identify individual differences, i.e., differences within a stakeholder group (those affected, family members, psychiatrists), 2.) explore differences between stakeholder groups, and 3.) examine possible intercultural differences between Israel and Germany.

interventions.name: The qualitative part of the study will involve focus groups to examine stigma and stereotypes among people with mental illness, family members/friends, and psychiatrists in connection with the use or non-use of antipsychotic medications. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
a) for service users 	
- Have first-hand experience with schizophrenia or psychosis
- Have current or past experience using or considering antipsychotics
b) for family/friends	
- Being a family member or friend of a service user who meets the criteria listed in a)		
c) for psychiatrists
- Experience as a psychiatrist with regard to the treatment of service users with psychosis or schizophrenia
While no specific diagnosis is required or given for service users, it is anticipated that the topic will be particularly relevant to individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia or psychotic disorders who are or have been undergoing psychiatric treatment. Nevertheless, as we aim to assess a spectrum of attitudes towards psychiatric treatment of psychosis, including critical attitudes, we do not want to exclude people who have been confronted with such a diagnosis personally, but do not accept it for themselves.
Exclusion criteria:
The only exclusion criterion results from the inclusion criterion that participants must be at least 18 years old, i. e. participants who are underage are excluded from the study.
